prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Square premium mature painterly Cantabrian folklore encyclopedia artwork of the FISH-MAN OF LIÉRGANES / Francisco de la Vega Casar at his legendary early return from the sea. Follow the documented description: one pale white-skinned young adult male with SHORT THIN RED HAIR, human-shaped head and body, a broad conspicuous vertical STRIP OF OVERLAPPING FISH SCALES running continuously from the front of his throat down the centre of his chest to his belly, and apparent GILL OPENINGS on both sides of his neck. These are anatomical fish scales and actual recessed gill-like slits, never tattoos, painted skin or clothing. The scale strip and neck gills must be unmistakably visible and make the legendary amphibious anatomy clear, not an ordinary man. Three-quarter view standing on a wet rocky coast by the Bay of Cádiz at dusk, chest toward viewer with neck turned slightly so gill openings visible. A modest rough cloth covers waist, hips and thighs; no genitals or eroticism. Exactly one head, two natural arms and hands, two legs and feet, all hands and feet inside frame. Quiet distant withdrawn seaborne aura rather than hostile combat. Wet skin/scale texture, dark coastal sea, antique-gold horizon and deep forest-green shadows, sophisticated painterly brushwork. No fish tail, fins, webbed hands, horns, wings, fish head, additional limbs, invented hybrid anatomy, other people, nets constricting body, gore, text, border, signature or watermark. This is a folkloric interpretation of recorded scales and apparent gills; not a biological fact claim about a historical person.
